```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)   # melt() para el heatmap

select <- dplyr::select
filter <- dplyr::filter
mutate <- dplyr::mutate
```

```{r carga-y-construccion, include=FALSE}
divorcios <- read_csv("Datos/divorcios_total.csv")
violencia <- read_csv("Datos/violencia_total.csv")

violencia <- violencia %>%
  mutate(
    cod_depto         = floor(hec_deptomcpio / 100),
    vic_edad_clean    = ifelse(vic_edad > 110, NA, vic_edad),
    total_hijos_clean = ifelse(total_hijos == 99, NA, total_hijos)
  )

divorcios <- divorcios %>%
  mutate(cod_depto = DEPOCU)

vio_dep <- violencia %>%
  filter(!is.na(cod_depto), cod_depto != 99) %>%
  group_by(cod_depto) %>%
  summarise(
    violencia_total   = n(),
    edad_prom_victima = mean(vic_edad_clean,    na.rm = TRUE),
    hijos_prom        = mean(total_hijos_clean, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_mujeres       = mean(vic_sexo == 2,      na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    pct_urbano        = mean(hec_area == 1,       na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    pct_casados       = mean(vic_est_civ == 2,    na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

div_dep <- divorcios %>%
  filter(!is.na(cod_depto), cod_depto != 99) %>%
  group_by(cod_depto) %>%
  summarise(casos_divorcio = n(), .groups = "drop")

datos_modelo <- vio_dep %>%
  inner_join(div_dep, by = "cod_depto") %>%
  mutate(es_capital = as.integer(cod_depto == 1))
```

# Matriz de Correlación — Variables del Modelo

## Dataset completo (22 departamentos)

```{r cor-completa, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=6.5, fig.cap="Correlaciones de Pearson entre todas las variables del modelo (n = 22 departamentos). La diagonal muestra el nombre de cada variable."}
vars_cor <- c("casos_divorcio", "violencia_total", "edad_prom_victima",
              "hijos_prom", "pct_mujeres", "pct_urbano", "pct_casados")

mat_cor <- cor(datos_modelo[, vars_cor], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Tabla numérica
kable(round(mat_cor, 2),
      caption = "Matriz de correlación de Pearson (dataset completo, n = 22)")
```

```{r heatmap-completo, fig.height=5, fig.width=6, fig.cap="Heatmap de correlaciones — dataset completo. Azul intenso = correlación positiva fuerte; rojo intenso = correlación negativa fuerte."}
mat_melt <- melt(mat_cor)

ggplot(mat_melt, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), size = 3, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low      = "#C0392B",
    mid      = "white",
    high     = "#2980B9",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits   = c(-1, 1),
    name     = "Pearson r"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Correlaciones de Pearson (n = 22 departamentos)",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
  )
```

---

## Sin el Departamento de Guatemala (21 departamentos)

Para evaluar cuánto influye la capital en las correlaciones, repetimos el
análisis excluyendo ese departamento.

```{r cor-sin-capital, fig.height=5, fig.width=6, fig.cap="Heatmap de correlaciones sin el Departamento de Guatemala (n = 21). Permite ver las relaciones reales en el interior del país."}
datos_sin_cap <- datos_modelo %>% filter(cod_depto != 1)

mat_cor2 <- cor(datos_sin_cap[, vars_cor], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

kable(round(mat_cor2, 2),
      caption = "Matriz de correlación de Pearson (sin Guatemala, n = 21)")
```

```{r heatmap-sin-capital, fig.height=5, fig.width=6, fig.cap="Heatmap sin la capital."}
mat_melt2 <- melt(mat_cor2)

ggplot(mat_melt2, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), size = 3, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low      = "#C0392B",
    mid      = "white",
    high     = "#2980B9",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits   = c(-1, 1),
    name     = "Pearson r"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlaciones de Pearson (sin Depto. Guatemala, n = 21)",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
  )
```

---

## Comparación directa de correlaciones con `casos_divorcio`

```{r comparacion-cor, fig.height=3.5, fig.cap="Correlación de cada predictor con casos_divorcio: dataset completo (azul) vs. sin Guatemala (naranja). Muestra cuánto depende la correlación de ese único departamento."}
comp_cor <- tibble(
  Variable    = vars_cor[-1],
  Completo    = mat_cor["casos_divorcio",  vars_cor[-1]],
  Sin_capital = mat_cor2["casos_divorcio", vars_cor[-1]]
) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Variable, names_to = "Dataset", values_to = "r")

ggplot(comp_cor, aes(x = reorder(Variable, abs(r)), y = r, fill = Dataset)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", alpha = 0.85, width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Completo" = "#2980B9", "Sin_capital" = "#E67E22"),
    labels = c("Con Guatemala (n=22)", "Sin Guatemala (n=21)")
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlación con casos_divorcio por predictor",
    x = NULL, y = "Pearson r", fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"))
```
